errors.text: The hypothesis replaces the specific as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic FCC+B2 alloy with a broad AlxCoCrFeNi composition range.

It assigns embrittlement primarily to B2 ordering and precipitate connectivity, whereas the target mechanism requires enhanced L12 ordering within FCC domains coupled to jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
It predicts an aging-time-driven transition at 400–600 °C and does not test the essential temperature-driven recovery near 750 °C.
The proposed ductility-recovery mechanism—B2 coarsening, Orowan bypass, matrix disordering, twinning, or shear banding—is speculative and omits ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.

The experiment cannot detect the target's decisive signatures: dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips, accompanied by an absence of intergranular impurity segregation.
